harness.system_prompt:
You are helm, an agent at the conn of the JobyCorp fleet. Be direct and concise.

Working method: survey before you read. `tree` shows where the mass is, `outline` gives a file's skeleton, `grep` with `context` replaces a read after every hit, `sgrep` answers structural questions (call sites, shapes), and `read` windows are for judgment, not indexing. Files go through the file tools: `read` not cat/sed, `grep` not grep/rg, `glob` not find, `edit`/`write` not sed or heredocs. Bash runs things: builds, tests, mix tasks. Dev servers and long commands run with `bash(background: true)`; `job` polls and kills them. Never signal a process you did not start. Commands must not wait on stdin: pass scripts with `-e` or a file, never an interactive `iex`. Read enough to act, act, verify, and stop.

harness.brief:
# JobyCorp website — design brief

JobyKit is already installed and `benchapp` is a generated JobyKit app that
compiles, boots, and passes its tests. Work inside `benchapp`. Follow the
guidelines in `AGENTS.md` and the design direction in `DESIGN.md`, both at
the project root; where `DESIGN.md` and this brief differ, this brief wins.

## The client

JobyCorp is a local AI research company. It runs analysis and benchmarks of
local LLMs on its own hardware and shares the research openly with the
community. The site is JobyCorp's public home: it should tell a visitor
what JobyCorp does, show that the work is real and rigorous, and invite
them to read and follow it.

Use only the facts above. Do not invent statistics, customer names, team
members, awards, dates, or product names. Where a section wants a number
or a name you have not been given, write copy that does not need one.

## Scope

This is a design task. Build the visual identity, the layout, the copy, and
the components. Do not add application features: no forms that submit, no
live data, no countdowns, no database. Static content and navigation only.

1. Remove every trace of the generator's demo: the stock `simple_nav`
   header, the "built with" footer, the welcome content of HomeLive, and
   every link to `/design`, `/custom-designs`, and `/design.json`. Those
   pages exist for inspecting the kit and are not part of the product;
   leave their routes in place but nothing on the site may link to or
   mention them.
2. Three pages, all on the same layout: `/` (the landing page),
   `/research` (what JobyCorp publishes and how it tests), and `/about`
   (who JobyCorp is and why the work is shared).
3. A top navigation bar in `Layouts.app` with id `main-nav` that marks the
   current page's link with `aria-current="page"`, collapses behind a
   toggle button with id `nav-toggle` at phone widths, and carries the
   kit's theme toggle with id `theme-toggle`, usable at both widths.
4. A footer that belongs to JobyCorp.
5. The landing page: a hero that says what JobyCorp does in one sentence, a
   section on the research (what is measured and how), a section on the
   hardware and method (local models, local hardware, results published in
   full), and a closing call to action to read the research. Sections are
   yours to add or merge; every section must earn its place.
6. At least one composite component of your own, registered in the
   DesignManifest with a `/design` preview, used on more than one page.

## Design requirements

- Light and dark themes, both finished, with the palette `DESIGN.md`
  defines applied to the `light` and `dark` themes in `app.css` (keep
  those two names; the theme toggle switches by them). Phone and desktop,
  both finished. No horizontal overflow at 390 px. Body text contrast at
  least 4.5:1 and large text at least 3:1 in both themes.
- Every icon name you use must exist in the installed heroicon set; check
  before you use it. A blank icon is a defect.
- Copy is concise: headings of a few words, sentences a visitor can read
  at a glance. Copy is about JobyCorp and its research, never about the
  component kit, the framework, or this task.
- Compose the kit's registered wrappers; raw HTML primitives are a lint
  failure. Lint must be clean.

## Tests

7. Existing tests must pass; update any test that referred to removed
   demo content. No new features. Add a render test for each new page.

## Constraints

- The dev server must run on port 4099; `PORT` is already set. Do not use
  any other port. Do not stop or kill processes you did not start.
- When `mix precommit` and `mix joby_kit.lint` both pass, reply with a
  one-line summary. Do not re-verify: green precommit and clean lint are the
  finish line.

Both finish-line gates are green (`mix precommit`: warnings-as-errors compile, no unused deps, formatted, 14 tests / 0 failures; `mix joby_kit.lint`: clean), and the dev server is running on port 4099.

JobyCorp now ships a paper-set three-page site — serif identity with the ink-blue palette in light and dark, a `main-nav` header (aria-current, `nav-toggle`, `theme-toggle`) and JobyCorp footer in `Layouts.app`, a landing hero whose record definition-list and monospace quantity figure are carried by two new registered composites (`record_list`, `specimen`) reused across `/`, `/research`, and `/about`, all demo chrome gone, with render tests per page and no overflow at 390 px.

desktop.text:
JobyCorp
Home
Research
About
A local AI research company that publishes what it runs

JobyCorp analyses and benchmarks local language models — models you can run on your own machine — on hardware it owns and operates. It is not a model vendor, a hosting service, or a benchmark for hire. The work is the research, and the research is shared with the community.

Why the work is shared

A number that arrives without its method asks the reader to trust a stranger. Publishing the machine, the prompts, and the settings alongside every measurement gives a reader something to check, and something specific to disagree with. Both are worth more than confidence.

Local models are built by people who handed over their weights and their code. Measuring them on our own machines and keeping the results to ourselves would be the odd choice.

What sharing looks like
Every run
the runs that went well and the runs that did not
The method
the harness, the prompts, and the settings behind every figure
The machine
what a run needed, and the limits it hit
The records
kept in full, never summarised down to a headline

All of it is on the research page, in the form it is kept in.

JobyCorp

JobyCorp runs local language models on its own hardware, measures them, and publishes the results in full.

desktop.text:
JobyCorp
Home
Research
About
We benchmark local language models on the hardware we own.

JobyCorp is an AI research company. We run local models on our own machines, measure what they do, and share the work with anyone who wants to read it.

What every record carries
Model
the model and its exact revision
Hardware
the machine the run was made on
Method
the harness, the prompts, the settings
Measured
what was timed and counted
Data
where the full result lives
What we measure

Every model is measured on the same harness, so a run can be read against the runs beside it. We time how long a prompt waits for its first token, how fast the answer arrives, how much of the machine the model takes up, and how the whole thing behaves as the prompt grows.

time to first token  ms
generation speed     tokens/s
peak memory          GiB
prompt length        tokens


Each quantity leaves with its unit, so a figure is never the only thing there.

How a run is set up, repeated, and written out is on the research page.

Local models on local hardware

Everything JobyCorp reports runs on machines we own and can see the front of. Nothing is measured through somebody else's endpoint, so no result depends on a server farm being quiet that afternoon.

The method travels with the number. A record names the model and its revision, the machine it ran on, the prompts it was given, the settings those prompts ran under, and the measurements taken — all of it, not the flattering parts.

Every result is published

The records, the method behind them, and the quantities they carry are on the research page.

Read the research
Who runs the machines

desktop.text:
JobyCorp
Home
Research
About
How the work is done, and what it leaves behind

JobyCorp publishes run records. Each one carries a measurement and everything needed to read it: the machine, the method, the quantities, and the units they came in. This page is that method, written out.

What we publish

A record is a result with its surroundings attached. It is written as the run happens, not reconstructed afterwards, and it leaves in the form it was kept in.

Model
which model ran, at the revision it was pulled at
Hardware
the machine it ran on, in the configuration it ran in
Method
the harness, the prompts, and every setting the run depended on
Measured
the quantities timed and counted, each with its unit
Data
where the full record lives and how to read it

A run that went badly is published on the same terms as one that went well. A result only carries weight if the failures beside it do too.

What we measure

The same quantities for every model, so a run can be read against the runs beside it. Timing runs from the request to the last token. Memory is the peak the model reached while it was working, not the size of its weights.

Prompt length is measured alongside them, because a figure taken on a short prompt says little about a long one. Where a quantity cannot be taken fairly, it is left out and the reason is written in the record.

How a run is published

Every run goes through the same four steps, in this order.

Set up
One model, one machine, one harness. The prompts and the settings are chosen and written down before anything runs.
Run
The model is given those prompts and timed, from the request to the last token.
Repeat
The run is done more than once. Every repeat is kept, so the record shows what varied rather than the best of it.
Publish
The record goes out with its method, so a reader can check the work or argue with it.
JobyCorp

JobyCorp runs local language models on its own hardware, measures them, and publishes the results in full.
